summary: Phase 0 of the myidsan productization plan: a batch of truth-and-hygiene fixes across shared infra and myidsan. The dead RequirePKCE/AllowRefreshToken/RefreshTokenTTLSeconds controls are removed from the Apps form and admin API (nothing in the authorize/token flow ever read them; the entity columns stay, reserved, for the future OIDC-conformance phase). The shared `loginSecurity` config block is now read only through a resolver that treats an absent block as ON with tuned defaults -- previously an absent block silently decoded to Enabled=false, which is what shipped in deploy/dist/myseliasan-config.json and the myidsan/myseliasan dev configs, making the failed-login lockout a silent no-op on those installs. `sso.internalToken` (guards /api/sso/introspect) is now refused at boot if it is a known placeholder value (it shipped as the literal `change-me-in-production` in myidsan's config files and had no such guard before); a placeholder is dropped rather than carried forward, disabling the endpoint instead of leaving a publicly-known token protecting it. Eight committed TLS private keypairs (all four apps) are untracked and apps/*/certs/ is now gitignored; real secrets (jwt secret, admin123, an internal-token placeholder, a live Google OAuth client_id) are scrubbed from apps/myidsan/config.json/config.dev.json. Swagger UI is now fully self-hosted (vendored swagger-ui-dist, served via go:embed) instead of loading from cdn.jsdelivr.net, which previously broke /swagger on air-gapped installs and violated the apps' own script-src 'self' CSP even when the CDN was reachable. Correctness/security fixes: myidsan's default-login path no longer discloses account state (disabled, federated-only) before a password has been verified -- an unknown username and a federated-only account both pay the cost of a dummy bcrypt compare so the timing and error are indistinguishable from a wrong password, and legacy plaintext password/SSO-internal-token comparisons are now constant-time; the federated-login continue-path sanitizer now rejects a backslash-prefixed open-redirect bypass (`/\evil.example`) that browsers normalise into a navigable host; toast `kind:'danger'` (matched no CSS class) is corrected to `'error'` at all 7 call sites; bulk-delete on Groups/Roles/Endpoints now asks for confirmation. A new CI workflow (`.github/workflows/go-check.yml`) runs build/vet/test on every push/PR plus an advisory govulncheck, and caught a stale test that had been failing unnoticed (fixed in infra/apphost/run_test.go).
compatibility: No schema changes. Existing installs that already set loginSecurity.enabled explicitly (true or false) are unaffected; only installs that omitted the block flip from an effective off to an effective on for the failed-login lockout -- this is the intended fix, not a regression, since the omission was never a deliberate choice to disable it. An install whose sso.internalToken is still the shipped placeholder loses working /api/sso/introspect access until an operator sets a real value (logged as a WARNING at boot); no relying app in this suite currently depends on that endpoint by default. requirePkce/allowRefreshToken/refreshTokenTtlSeconds silently stop round-tripping through the Apps form and admin API for any deployment that happened to set them, since they were never enforced -- no behavior changes for anyone who wasn't already relying on validation that didn't exist. TLS certs/keys are regenerated on first boot if missing, as before; untracking them from git does not affect a running install. Swagger UI now requires no internet access; nothing else about /swagger's URL or JSON contract changed.
